validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: the sheet's own cited ref (liting.uz/page/4, 'История института' i.e. the O'zLITIneftgaz design institute's history page) is a React SPA that serves an empty <div id=root> shell server-side -- our url_verifier's '200 but data value not found' result is a rendering artifact, not evidence the page lacks the content; I could not find a public API backing it or a Wayback capture of that specific path (only the site root is archived), so I could not read it directly. Rather than accept that on faith, I searched independently in Russian for 'Мубарек-Каган' газопровод outside GEM. AO 'Мубарекнефтегазмонтаж' (Mubarekneftegazmontazh) -- the pipeline-construction/assembly company headquartered in Mubarek, with a dedicated fabrication unit in Kagan district of Bukhara region -- names 'газопровод «Мубарек - Каган»' (verbatim) twice on its own company-history page, in the same sentence listing the Mubarek gas-processing plant, several condensate fields, the Bukhara oil refinery and the Sazakino-Nukus pipeline as facilities it built/serviced (http://www.mngmaj.uz/about/index.htm, url_verifier OK on 'Мубарек'+'Каган'+'Мубарекнефтегазмонтаж'). That is a genuinely independent, non-GEM, non-abarrelfull source affirmatively naming this exact pipeline as a real built object. Second, weaker corroboration: the UNDP-published 'Схема газотранспортной системы Республики Узбекистан' (Outlook for Renewable Energy in Uzbekistan, Appendix 1, p.89 -- the same PDF GEM's own wiki page cites as ref [2]) is a 300dpi schematic map, not full-text (pdftotext extracts only the caption; the verifier's automated substring check correctly FAILs on it -- I rendered it to PNG at 300dpi and read it visually per the project's map-reading convention). It shows a multi-line (3-4 parallel strands) trunk bundle running the Bukhara/Kagan hub<->Mubarek corridor -- consistent with, though not name-specific proof of, a Mubarek-Kagan pipeline (the map doesn't print a 'Kagan' label separately from 'Бухара', since the town is essentially adjacent to Bukhara). Net: existence is corroborated by one strong independent naming source plus one supporting schematic -- tier medium (not high, since only one source actually names the pipeline). CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is right -- this line carries processed gas out of the Mubarek gas-processing plant (МГПЗ, labeled on the UNDP map at Мубарек) into the Bukhara/Kagan hub for onward distribution via the Gazli-Kagan and BTBA trunks, i.e. a trunk/transmission role, not a wellhead gathering line. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the roster: P6965 (Mubarek-Kagan I) is the obvious candidate, but per the country's Kazakhstan-cluster-A lesson, a shared corridor + shared endpoints is NOT itself proof of a double count -- no source I found describes Mubarek-Kagan I and II as one pipe, and the UNDP map's multi-line bundle is physically consistent with two (or more) genuinely parallel strings, matching the pattern of every other Kagan/Gazli/Mubarek pipeline family in this country (Gazli-Kagan I-IV, BTBA I-III). Not flagging as duplicate. Also checked against Gazli-Kagan (P2290/P3983/P3984, a different corridor converging on the same Bukhara/Kagan hub from the NW) and Kelif-Mubarek (P6936, a different pipeline entirely, Kelif->Mubarek not Mubarek->Kagan) -- no overlap. SPEC: Length/Diameter/Capacity are blank on the sheet and I could not source string-level values for either Mubarek-Kagan I or II anywhere, including GEM's own wiki page (which also leaves these blank for both segments) -- Uztransgaz does not publish a line-wise register. Per this country's calibration (between India and Kazakhstan), a genuine Russian-language search that comes up empty on a per-string spec is the correct UNRESOLVED outcome here, not a gap I manufactured a number to fill. ATTRIBUTION: StartLocation=Mubarek/EndLocation=Kagan, both Uzbekistan, confirmed by the independent mngmaj.uz source and by the UNDP map; Operator=Uztransgaz (from GEM's own wiki, not independently re-verified here since Operator isn't a unit on this worklist and lives on the separate operators/owners tab per the country note). StartState/Province and EndState/Province were blank and are filled below.

Downgraded from REFS_ADDED: both refs were Wikipedia infoboxes. The underlying facts are routine gazetteer lookups (Mubarek -> Qashqadaryo region/Muborak district; Kagan/Kogon -> Bukhara region) and should be cited from GeoNames, which is the established substitute in this repo (Egypt P8022/P8023/P8049 used GeoNames for Abu Madi). The mngmaj.uz company page corroborating Mubarek's 180900 postal code is itself citable. Prior note: StartLocation Mubarek and EndLocation Kagan were already on the sheet with no admin-region breakdown. Muborak's Wikipedia infobox gives Region=Qashqadaryo Region, District=Muborak District (postal code 180900, matching the address on mngmaj.uz's own company page, which is HQ'd in Mubarek). Kagan (Kogon)'s infobox gives Region=Bukhara Region; note Kagan is itself a district-level city and only the SEAT of (not administratively part of) Kogon District, so I did not fill EndPrefecture/District to avoid asserting a debatable subdivision -- StartPrefecture/District left blank for the same reason of consistency (no other Uzbekistan row in this tracker currently uses this field, unlike ~30% of rows tracker-wide in other countries). Both sources are Wikipedia infoboxes for uncontroversial administrative geography, not independent origins from each other in the strict corroboration sense -- tier medium, independent=false, flagged honestly rather than inflated to high.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No dated news, incident report, decommissioning notice, or reconstruction announcement for 'Мубарек-Каган' turned up in either English or Russian search (2025-2026 window searched specifically). The only currently-live independent evidence is AO Mubarekneftegazmontazh's own company-profile page (accessed 2026-08-26), which lists the Mubarek-Kagan pipeline among the trunk facilities it built and continues to offer capital-repair/maintenance services for ('Капитальный ремонт технологических установок и инженерных коммуникаций' is listed among its current service lines) -- the page itself is undated (a standing corporate history, not a news item), so this is weak/indirect recency evidence, not a dated confirmation. This is a mature Soviet-era-descended trunk feeding gas from the Mubarek GPZ into the Bukhara/Kagan hub, i.e. core existing infrastructure with no plausible reason to have gone offline and no evidence that it has; verdict is 'confirm' but flagged as low-confidence on the DATE specifically, high-confidence on the fact of continued operation. Did not find independent evidence dated after the sheet's own 2024-09 LastUpdated, so this does not clear the bar for a 'change' and there is no basis for 'stale' either (this is not a proposed/shelved-clock row).
